blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: Fraction Fitness
blocks.content: Adding fractions is one of the most fundamental skills in math, yet it trips up students at every level. This gym drills you on rapid-fire fraction addition until finding common denominators becomes second nature.

blocks.title: 2. The Rules: Same Denominator Required
blocks.content:
You can ONLY add fractions when they have the same denominator.

• If denominators match: just add the numerators. 3/7 + 2/7 = 5/7.
• If denominators differ: find the LCM of both denominators first.
• Convert both fractions to equivalent fractions with that LCM.
• Then add the numerators.

blocks.title: 3. The Method: Quick LCM Trick
blocks.content:
For two fractions a/b + c/d where b and d are different:

1. Cross multiply: new numerator 1 = a * d, new numerator 2 = c * b.
2. New denominator = b * d.
3. Add: (ad + cb) / (bd).
4. Simplify the result by dividing top and bottom by their GCD.

blocks.title: 4. Worked Example: Adding Unlike Fractions
blocks.content:
Calculate 2/3 + 3/4.

**Step 1:** Cross multiply: 2*4 = 8, 3*3 = 9.
**Step 2:** Common denominator: 3*4 = 12.
**Step 3:** 8/12 + 9/12 = 17/12.
**Step 4:** Convert: 17/12 = 1 and 5/12.

**Final Answer: 1 5/12.**

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: NEVER add the denominators! 2/3 + 3/4 is NOT 5/7. This is the most common fraction mistake in all of mathematics. You need a COMMON denominator first, then only the numerators get added. The denominator stays the same after addition.
